_missing.title: Worn Stone
_missing.body: Whatever was written here has been rained on for too long. Only the shape of the letters remains, and they are not letters anyone still reads.

grave_marker.title: Grave Marker
grave_marker.body: No name. Only a shallow groove where a candle stood until the wax ran out. Someone dug this grave for you, and did not wait to see you climb out of it.

chapel_inscription.title: Chapel Lintel
chapel_inscription.body: When the water warms, ring the bells in the order the dead were laid down. The dead were laid down in the order they stopped tending the fire. Nobody tends it now.

sluice_notice.title: Sluice House Notice
sluice_notice.body: The wheel is kept elsewhere by order of the lord, for the pond must not be drained while the thing beneath it still sleeps. If it wakes, draining it will not matter.

shrine_verse.title: Candle Shrine Verse
shrine_verse.body: A wick exists to carry flame, and flame exists to be carried down. We lit these candles so the Hearth would know the way back up. It has not looked up in a long time.

windmill_verse.title: Windmill Verse
windmill_verse.body: The sails turned while the wind had something to say. Now the wind only remembers. One syllable of the Name is carved where the miller could see it from his bed.

crypt_verse.title: Crypt Verse
crypt_verse.body: The living let the Name go one letter at a time, and the dead picked them up. Lie still beside them a while and you will hear a coffin lid repeating the first.

grave_sluice_keeper.title: Headstone, Moss-Eaten
grave_sluice_keeper.body: OSWIN, who kept the sluice and rang the sluice bell when the water rose. Laid down in the third year of the Quiet, the first of us to stop tending. He said the pond would keep. It has.

grave_gatekeeper.title: Headstone, Leaning
grave_gatekeeper.body: ALDRIC, who kept the gate and rang the gate bell at dusk. Laid down in the seventh year of the Quiet, after Oswin and before Maud. The lord took his key and shut the gate from the inside.

grave_watch.title: Headstone, Newest
grave_watch.body: MAUD of the watch, who rang the keep's bell while there was still someone to warn. Laid down in the eleventh year of the Quiet, the last of us. Nobody tends the fire now, and nobody rings.

village_lane_stone.title: Lane Stone
village_lane_stone.body: The lane ran from the pond up to the castle, and the ash came down it the other way. Seven houses and a store. The thatch went first, then the people, and the dogs stopped waiting at the doors.

_comment: DRAFT (O-3): the entries from maren_tally down are W8-H house inscriptions pending the owner's sign-off. pond_shrine_verse hides a syllable in its mid-sentence capitals (A, S, H as a placeholder); the owner should make it agree with the crypt's syllable, since the Vale's fragment of the Name lives in the crypt.

maren_tally.title: Gravekeeper's Tally
maren_tally.body: Scratched into the hearth wall, one line a grave. Nine by the pond, all of a depth. The tenth was dug ahead of need, for a pilgrim who said he would come back this way. He did not say when.

pond_shrine_verse.title: Shrine Tablet
pond_shrine_verse.body: wake it Alone, when the Sun is down, and Hum what the pond hums back to you. Do not bring a lamp. It has seen enough of fire that goes out.

road_cottage_lintel.title: Door Lintel
road_cottage_lintel.body: Locked from the outside, and the key gone with whoever turned it. Below the lock, newer and shallower: 'gone to the farms for the sowing. back by first frost.' There have been many frosts.

north_watch_stone.title: Watch Stone
north_watch_stone.body: From here you could see the castle, the village and the pond in one turn of the head, and the fire under none of them. The watch kept watching anyway. That is what a watch is.

east_shrine_tablet.title: Toll-Men's Tablet
east_shrine_tablet.body: The toll-men prayed here before the gate and after it. What they could not carry past the castle they left with the saint: a coin, a name, once a key. The saint keeps what it is given.

edge_shrine_tablet.title: Edge Tablet
edge_shrine_tablet.body: This is as far as the land goes and as far as he went. A sword laid on an altar is a prayer that the next hand will need it less. Take it. The prayer was not answered the first time.

villager_smith.title: The Smith
villager_smith.body: Iron I have. Charcoal I have. What I have not had in four years is a reason, and you do not look like one.

villager_miller.title: The Miller
villager_miller.body: The wheel turns on wind now. There has been no water in that race since the pond went down, and I grind nothing but talk.

villager_herder.title: The Herder
villager_herder.body: Six left, of forty. They will not go near the water, and I have stopped making them.

villager_widow.title: The Widow
villager_widow.body: They went up the road to the castle to ask for help. That was the asking. There was no coming back.

villager_boy.title: The Lamplighter
villager_boy.body: I light them at dusk and they are out by morning, every one. Something walks the street and does not like the light.

villager_carter.title: The Carter
villager_carter.body: The ox died standing in the traces. I have not had the heart to unhitch him, so the cart stays where it is.

villager_elder.title: The Elder
villager_elder.body: You are the first through the gate in a long while. Mind that we are the sort of place people pass through.

villager_watch.title: The Watchman
villager_watch.body: There is nothing to watch for. I watch anyway. It is the last thing anyone asked me to do.

villager_digger.title: The Gravedigger
villager_digger.body: I dig them two at a time now. It saves walking back for the spade.

villager_wife.title: At the Well
villager_wife.body: Draw if you like. It comes up clean, which is the only thing in this valley that still does.

thornhollow_pyre.title: The Village Pyre
thornhollow_pyre.body: They keep the fire in the middle and the stones at the edge. Ask them which came first and they will tell you the stones, and that the stones were standing before anyone was counting.

thorn_warden.title: The Warden of the Gap
thorn_warden.body: You came through the gap. Nobody comes through the gap. Go back the way you came, and do not tell the road about us.

thorn_child.title: The Child
thorn_child.body: There is a wall of trees, and then there is us. I have never been past the trees. Father says that past the trees it is all roads.

thorn_fletcher.title: The Fletcher
thorn_fletcher.body: Shafts out of the wood, heads out of the old field. We have no smith. We have never needed one and we do not want the noise.

thorn_herder.title: The Herder
thorn_herder.body: Four goats and the stones. The stones keep the wolves out better than any fence I ever set, and I have set a great many fences.

thorn_widow.title: The Widow
thorn_widow.body: My husband went out to find where the river went. The river goes to the end of the world. He should have asked me.

wyrms_rest.title: Wyrm's Rest
wyrms_rest.body: It came down in the long year and it has not moved since. We fenced it so the children would stop climbing the ribs, and then we raised a stone, so as not to look like people who only build fences.

sunken_wheel.title: The Sunken Wheel
sunken_wheel.body: A wheel of worked stone, eight paces across, standing on its edge and sinking. There is writing at the foot of it and the writing has gone. Whoever cut this did not cut it for us.
